summary.tldr: Creates a new process for reviewing misconduct by federally appointed judges and changes how removal recommendations are made.
what_it_does: Replaces the process the Canadian Judicial Council uses to review conduct complaints about federally appointed judges.
Creates a new process for allegations of misconduct that are not serious enough to lead to a judge’s removal from office.
Changes the process for making recommendations to remove a judge and send them to the Minister of Justice.
Applies the same process to certain office holders, other than judges, who are appointed by Parliament to serve during good behaviour.
summary.background: The bill amends the Judges Act. It replaces the current process used to review the conduct of federally appointed judges.
